least_run.text: Credibility: has taken hundreds of these calls
Asks if anything else is getting in the way
Asks if there is anything else they should know
Paints getting started before revealing the investment
Tie-down: 'not should I, but how do I make this work'
Goes deeper with a segment-aware cost question
States the price and stays silent
Uses the 1 to 10 scale when the answer is uncertain
Flexes the call to the segment (novice, achiever, rebuilder, returner)

I've seen a lot of people like, reconnect with their exes, too.

I do genuinely believe like what we do here is something that can 100% help you and then genuinely get you to, to your end goal.
80% of the people that she helps within a year, they find someone and they're in a healthy relationship.

top_flags.summary: Rep had the prospect read his Social Security number, DOB, phone, address and income aloud on a recorded call and typed them into financing on her own shared screen.
After the prospect asked for a day or two, said he felt rushed and said he felt pressured, the rep kept pushing with false urgency over the credit pull and told him he would not get anywhere.
Rep told the prospect to state at least $30,000 annual income on the ClarityPay loan application after he said he made $18,000.
Prospect disclosed depression, autism, no income and fear; rep sold through it into a 24-month financed loan with no pause or care check.
Rep quoted packages that aren't in the sanctioned offer: a $7-14K range over 3-12 months, $2,400 for 6 weeks/4 sessions, then $1K for two sessions.
Rep quoted relationship success rates (50% in six months, 78% in 12 months) and K. attending client weddings as part of the pitch.
Rep cited an unverified 80% figure for clients meeting their life partner within a year, alongside the price quote.
Rep improvised a $1,000 non-refundable deposit for a trial call with K., framed as 'pulling strings' with the financial team; not part of the sanctioned offer.
Rep framed K. as treating trauma, and when the prospect assumed K. is a licensed therapist and asked about insurance, she did not correct him and offered to ask.
Rep made shaming armchair diagnoses and kept pushing financing after the prospect said his finances were dire.
Rep offered an unsanctioned 6-week, 4-session package at $2,400.
Rep cited specific relationship success rates and said the program will get her the results she wants, which strongly implies a relationship outcome.
Rep framed coaching as getting him to marriage and tied the $7,200 price to 'get you to your goal of finding someone, getting married'.
Improvised a $4,000 bi-weekly 3-month tier (sanctioned is $3,600) and a $1,000 first-call deposit credited toward $7,200 after a value objection.
Rep cited success statistics for finding a partner and guaranteed he would reach his goal.
Rep told him the $364 monthly financing meant he would not be charged more, though 24 payments of $364 exceed the $7,200 price, and claimed approvals need Kimberly's sign-off.
Rep claimed 80%+ of clients find their life partner within the first year to build belief before the pitch.
Rep improvised a $1,000 single-call 'deposit' that isn't in the sanctioned offer, then split it into installments and took $100.
Rep promised the prospect Kimberly would find him a partner and keep him out of bad relationships, and quoted relationship-rate stats.

Prospect disclosed past physical abuse, ongoing mental-health struggles, a disability, job loss and medical costs; the rep acknowledged it briefly and kept pushing for payment with no care or referral.
After the prospect said many times he couldn't commit or afford it, the rep kept pressing, claimed she was 'pulling some strings', and insisted he pay on the call.
Rep quoted a $3,400 three-month bi-weekly option (sanctioned tier 1.5 is $3,600) and an improvised in-house $500/month plan spread over about 7 months.
Rep offered the full three-month weekly 1:1 program for $3,500, about half the sanctioned $7,200 price, and agreed to send an agreement.
After disclaiming guarantees, rep cited relationship success rates and told the prospect K. will get her the result she wants (marriage).
Rep offered an unsanctioned 6-week package at about $2,400, splittable, and misstated the programs as 6-12 months at $7K-$14K.
Rep quoted unsanctioned prices: $3,800 for six bi-weekly calls over 3 months (sanctioned is $3,600) and a $1K two-call package she says she doesn't usually offer.
Rep claimed over 80% of clients find their partner within a year.
Rep improvised two months of coaching for $4,500 after the prospect asked for a discount, and offered $4,500 now with the balance 'worked out' later.
Rep quoted 50%/78% relationship rates and K. attending client weddings, and framed the price as getting him to marriage.

Prospect disclosed depression and that failure would mean increasing his medication and hating himself; rep used this as cost-of-inaction leverage and later to push for a same-day decision, with no care or referral.

Prospect disclosed a trauma-related stress disorder, depression and not being ready to date; the rep reframed his readiness as something to act through and went on to pitch and probe his finances without checking his support.
Rep cited an 80% rate of men meeting their partner within the first year to push past a delivery doubt.
Rep improvised a $1K first-time payment for a single first call or first month, credited toward the full program; not a sanctioned tier.
Rep improvised a $500 'first call with K.' entry and a custom reduced plan that is not in the sanctioned offer.
Rep claimed over 80% of clients meet their ideal partner within six months.
Rep improvised a one-month / four-session product at $2,400 and took a ~$1,000 deposit for 'the first two calls'; CRM logs it as 'Foundation Program', $2,400 contract.
Rep quoted relationship-outcome statistics as part of the scripted pitch, despite a no-guarantee caveat.
Rep quoted six months at $13,900 (sanctioned $14,000), dumped all tiers, then sold an off-menu $1,000 one-time session with K. against a $5-$100 deposit.
Rep offered an unsanctioned 6-week, four-session package for about $2,400 and described programs of 3 to 12 months.
In response to a burned-before objection, rep claimed over 80% of clients find their life partner within a year.

calls.coach_note: When a prospect discloses past suicidality and sexual assault, pause, acknowledge with care and check safety before continuing, and never ask whether she 'presents herself' as someone men just want sex from; also run a temperature check before price and do not promise custom payment plans that do no

This close put a low-income, self-described depressed and autistic prospect into a 24-month 17% APR loan after the rep told him to overstate his income on the application; escalate immediately. Discovery was confrontational and age-shaming; the rep must not coach credit applications, call soft pulls

Discovery became confrontational: she diagnosed trauma and told the prospect he was 'emotionally very damaged' before pitching, then pressed a man describing dire finances. She also let him believe K. is a licensed therapist. Coach on the no-correction rule before the pitch, therapy boundaries, and

This call needs manager review: the rep collected the prospect's SSN aloud on a recorded call, guaranteed results, and kept pressing after he twice said he felt rushed and pressured. Retrain on outcome language, data handling and respecting a think-it-over request.

Do not invent deals (a non-refundable $1,000 trial-call deposit from the 'financial team') to resolve trust uncertainty; and when a prospect was earlier quoted about $1,200/month, offer the sanctioned $3,600 bi-weekly tier instead of losing him on the $7,200 tier.
The prospect called out the leading 'would you agree' questions mid-discovery, so swap those for open questions. Drop the 50%/78% relationship statistics and run a 1-10 check before stating price.

Prospect said four times he couldn't afford it right now and was between jobs; running a credit application by screen share and a 'limited spots' deposit ask was pushing past a clear no. Ask the problem question up front and let him answer before reframing.

Discovery circled the same desired-picture question until the prospect felt judged and demanded the price. Use the current four-pillar pitch, drop the relationship-rate statistics, and stop pushing a credit check once the prospect says she does not want more debt.

Rep pitched an outdated framework, never quoted a sanctioned tier, and improvised a $1,000 trial call paid down from $100 for a recently unemployed, disabled prospect who repeatedly said he couldn't commit. Coach on running discovery to the playbook, stopping when the prospect isn't a fit, and never

Strong frame and why-now work, but she reached for payment plans and an improvised $1,000 deposit at the first sign of uncertainty, then spent 30 minutes re-pushing after a clear 24-hour request. Run the 1-10 check before price and stop pitching alternatives once a prospect states a decision process

Rep repeated the 'fastest route' pitch three times instead of diagnosing the objection; she should have asked whether he believes the process would work for him and what trying on his own looks like, then tested a 'how would you make this work' tie-down.

Discovery skipped the problem and background phases, then used his depression and self-criticism as leverage and improvised a $4,500 two-month deal. Stick to the sanctioned tiers and don't use a prospect's mental-health disclosure as a closing lever.

Never improvise prices: after saying $7,200 was the only option, the rep discounted to half price for the full program, which undermines every other client. Use the sanctioned $3,600 bi-weekly tier for a firm budget, and drop relationship-rate stats and 'she's going to get you the result'.

When the temperature check returns 'I really don't know', stay there and scale it before price; never answer a value doubt with improvised $4,000 and $1,000 offers, and drop 'when we get you there... getting married' language.

Discovery was thorough, but the pitch was a read-out of the old framework with relationship-rate statistics, and price was two tiers with no recommendation. To a stated 'I don't decide on the spot' prospect, stacking payment options didn't help; isolate the real concern instead.

Discovery was thorough but the pitch was off-script (old framework, all tiers dumped, $13,900 instead of $14,000) and the close leaned on urgency and an improvised $1,000 single session with a token deposit. Recommend one tier after a real temperature check and do not invent off-menu products.

Strong discovery and a clean pitch, but quoting 50%/78% relationship rates breaks the no-outcome-promise rule. Ask the doubt question and confirm she has the full call time before the pitch so the close isn't cut by her next meeting.

Discovery was thorough but meandered for 90 minutes on a low-intent, low-budget prospect; qualify budget and intent early and release cleanly instead of using faith arguments to hold someone who has said no three times.

Discovery was long and circled her readiness for 40 minutes, and she twice had to ask for the price, which she read as pressure. Get the tie-down on timing before the pitch, name tiers accurately, and do not hold price hostage once the prospect asks.

The prospect disclosed a stress disorder from finding his sister dead, plus depression, and said he wasn't ready to date. The rep reframed that as 'take action despite it' and went on to a $14K close. On calls like this, check for support and readiness before selling, and quote the sanctioned tier t
Good handling: rep confirmed the full hour, explained why the call must be on video and recorded, and rebooked rather than rushing. Make sure the CRM records her as the closer.

Strong discovery and a clean temperature check, but the investment section unravelled: tier one was quoted as the 6-month 14K, then a $3,400 bi-weekly price that isn't on the sheet, then a custom $500/month plan. Quote the sanctioned tier that matches the recommendation and avoid naming other client

Discovery, temperature check and objection pacing were textbook. Fix the investment: 'Tier 1' was quoted at the Tier 2 price, and the close used a $3,400 bi-weekly price that isn't the sanctioned $3,600. Also add the recording and confidentiality disclosure to the opener.

Strong discovery and pitch structure, but she pitched $14k to a 21-year-old who had told the setter he couldn't invest and has no job or bank account; qualify finances before a 90-minute call. D.'t float '$100 a month' figures that don't fit the sanctioned tiers.
This was a strong, well-sequenced call. Two things to fix: add the recording disclosure, and never use another client's name and personal anxiety details as a proof story.

Discovery was strong, but the close turned into improvising: a split payment and an off-menu $1K session for a fear objection, plus a '99%' pressure stat and another client's mental-health story. Stay on the sanctioned tiers, name them correctly, and handle fear of K. before price.

Discovery was warm and thorough, but the finance signals were loud well before price and she was never qualified, so the $14k recommendation landed on someone living paycheck to paycheck. Disclose the recording, qualify capacity earlier and consider the 3-month tier when money is the stated constrai

Good tailored pillar walk-through, but price went out before the pitch and the 80%-find-a-partner line is an outcome claim. Once he said he had no money, asking him to open his bank account on the call was unnecessary; qualify finances earlier and exit gracefully.
Strong objection pacing, but price was dropped before the pillars and before any temperature check; keep the investment until after a 1-10 check and drop the '80% meet their life partner' line.

P. was dropped in the middle of the pitch, before any temperature check, and an 80% 'find your life partner within a year' stat was used as a sales lever. Finish the pitch, run the temperature check, then recommend one tier, and drop the outcome statistic.

When the prospect pushed for her personal romantic opinion, the rep engaged instead of holding a clear professional boundary. Under uncertainty she then used the 80% partner statistic and an improvised half-now payment split. Redirect personal questions firmly, and handle caution with a temperature

The rep never pitched the sanctioned offer and instead improvised a $3,800 six-call option and a $1K two-call starter because the prospect 'seemed hesitant'. Stick to the three sanctioned tiers. Treat hesitancy with the temperature check, not a cheaper product.

A defensible no-pitch on a newly separated, low-urgency prospect, but the frame (confidentiality, recording, credibility) and the cost and future-picture questions were skipped. Run C6/C7 fully before deciding not to pitch, and log him as a nurture lead with a date.

Strong, tailored pillar pitch, but price was dumped (both tiers) before the pitch and temperature check, and the close relied on an improvised one-month/$1K product. Drop the 80%-partner statistic and hold the sanctioned tiers.

P. came before the pitch and before any temperature check, then the delivery doubt was met with an improvised $1K trial and an 80% partner statistic. Uncover competing options and in-person requirements early, and handle uncertainty on belief, not on a cheaper entry point.

P. came first, before any pitch or temperature check, and the guarantee question was met with an 80% partner stat and an improvised trial month. Hold price until belief is confirmed, and answer 'guarantee' with the process promise only.

Hold price until after the pitch and temperature check, and quote the $7,200 tier as sanctioned (3 months weekly) rather than 'weekly or bi-weekly, 3 to 6 months', which blurs it with the $3,600 tier.

Control the frame early: run the intro (confidential, recorded, goal of the call) and interrupt long tangents with the discovery questions so the call reaches the temperature check before the price. D.'t improvise a one-month or single-session offer; hold the sanctioned tiers and book a proper secon

Pitch started with two prices before any temperature check or next-steps framing, and the close fell back on an improvised $500 first-call deposit that isn't in the offer. Run C1 framing, save belief-correction for the pitch, and hold one tier after the temperature check.

The prospect spent much of discovery describing her phone being hacked and women sabotaging her, which the rep herself suspected was paranoia, yet per the CRM the rep went on to pitch and try to take payment. Pause and make a wellbeing/fit decision before selling, disclose recording up front, and ne

The pitch covered the pillars, but Makena quoted an 80% partner success rate and cut the offer to a $2,400 first month when he was skeptical. Hold the 12-week recommendation, deal with trust before money, and never cite outcome rates.

Discovery was solid, but Makena gave the price at the start of the pitch and offered to split payments before he objected. Run the temperature check and next-steps picture first, then give one price and stay silent.

P. was dropped before the pitch and before any temperature check, then timing hesitancy was met with a $1K deposit and financial options instead of a belief check; frame the call (confidential, recorded) and hold price until the prospect rates the process.
Strong discovery, but the rep quoted an unsanctioned 6-week $2,400 package and price before the temperature check. Disclose recording at the start, and don't promise to delete it.

Before deciding not to pitch, run the why-now, cost and desired-picture questions: the post-rejection rumination and a pattern of choosing unavailable women were surfaced but never costed. Open with the confidentiality and recording frame.

Discovery was strong, but the rep improvised unsanctioned packages ($2,400 for 6 weeks, then $1K for two sessions) and quoted price inside the pitch before any temperature check. With get-my-ex-back leads, qualify out early and don't hint at reconciliation.

Makena pitched an unsanctioned $2,400 six-week package before discovery was finished and implied app results ('two dates a week'). Finish discovery and the desired-situation questions, and quote only sanctioned tiers.
Makena invented an unsanctioned $2,400 six-week package and stated price before any pillars or temperature check. Run the full pitch and temperature check, and stay within the sanctioned tiers.

With a known 45-minute hard stop, the rep spent the whole call in personal-history discovery (limerence, childhood, clutter) and never reached cost, future picture or the pitch. Manage the clock to reach C6 to C9, and avoid remarks like asking why he looks down while he is discussing something painf

Discovery depth was good, but she revealed price and the 14K tier before pitching and skipped the temperature check. She also passed over a self-harm reference without checking in. P. only after the pitch and the 1-10 check, and pause on any self-harm remark.

Discovery and pillar coverage were strong, but price came before the pitch and the close turned into a 30-minute push for a $50-$200 'commitment' from a prospect supporting family who had to leave for church. Run the temperature check before price and stop pushing once a genuine cash-flow constraint

Lead's messages went unanswered for about 3 days before a brief brush-off.
Lead sent detailed objections and nobody on the business side replied in this thread.

Setter quoted a specific price figure by text contrary to the range-anchor rule

Sender identity inconsistent: message from the 'Kimberly Rae' sender introduces itself as someone else, and the lead later says she never spoke to the setter and the claimed 15-minute call is not remembered.
Scarcity pitch ('rare opening with Kimberly herself') sent two days after the lead declined the offer in writing.
Closer discounted scope in chat for a $3,500 price after sending a checkout link; price and scope offered by text outside the setter range anchor.
Lead asked what the proposed follow-up meeting was for; next reply came ten days later and did not answer it.
